Windows Server 2012 R2 and 2016

If you’re currently running the legacy Microsoft Defender for Endpoint agent solution (based on the Microsoft Monitoring Agent - MMA) with MsSenseS.exe version 10.3720.*, please skip directly to Update path 2.


Update path 1

Update the latest EDR sensor version described in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint update for EDR Sensor using one of the following methods:
  • Windows Update
  • A patch management solution such as WSUS
  • Downloading and applying the package from the Microsoft Update Catalog.

Update path 2

This option only applies if you’re currently running the legacy Microsoft Defender for Endpoint agent solution (based on the Microsoft Monitoring Agent - MMA) with MsSenseS.exe version 10.3720.*, in which case you will first need to upgrade to the new solution by following these steps:
  1. Go to the onboarding page in the M365 Defender portal
  2. Select the ‘Windows Server 2012 R2 and 2016 (Preview)’ operating systems
  3. Choose your preferred deployment method
  4. Download the installation and onboarding packages
  5. Install the package and apply the onboarding script via your chosen deployment channel
  6. Once the new solution has been installed, future updates should be done by following the instructions described in Update path 1.
For additional information on what’s new and how to install, including applying Defender Antivirus passive mode configuration if you’re using a non-Microsoft antimalware solution,please refer to Onboard Windows servers to the Microsoft Defender for Endpoint service | Microsoft Docs.



Linux and macOS

To ensure continued protection, ensure that the MDE agent is in the 3 latest versions. However, it is recommended to update to the latest Microsoft Defender for Endpoint version listed in What's new in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint on Mac or What's new in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint on Linux using one of the following methods:
  • MacOS: Microsoft Auto Update. More details at Deploy updates for Microsoft Defender for Endpoint on macOS
  • Linux: Using the update command based on your distributions package manager. More details at Deploy updates for Microsoft Defender for Endpoint on Linux
  • Downloading and applying the package from the onboarding section of the security center portal for your respective OS.

For additional information on what’s new and how to install, please refer to Onboard non-Windows devices

Important: In centrally managed environments, locally created firewall rules may not be applied if local firewall rules are not allowed or local policy merge is disabled. If firewall policies are managed through Intune, MDM, or Group Policy, deploy the outbound block rule using the same centralized management channel.

Option 1: Using Intune for managed environments

  1. Go to Microsoft Intune admin center https://intune.microsoft.com
  2. Navigate to Endpoint security > Firewall > Firewall Policies > Create Policy
  3. Configure:
    1. Platform: windows
    2. Profile: Windows Firewall Rules
    3. Click Create
  4. In Basic Tab:
    1. Enter a name for the rule (e.g., "Block mshta.exe outbound connections") and optional description.
  5. Click Next for Configuration Settings:
    1. Click on Add for a new firewall rule and provide name
    2. Select Action as Block
    3. Select Edit instance and configure the following:
      1. Enabled -> Enabled
      2. Interface -> All
      3. File Path -> toggle to configured and add the path "%SystemRoot%\System32\mshta.exe"
      4. Direction -> Select "This rule applies to Outbound traffic"
      5. Leave all other fields as is "not configured"
      6. And Save
    4. For 64-bit systems, repeat steps (a) through (c) under the same policy. While doing so, update the FilePath in step (c)(iii) to: %systemroot%\syswow64\mshta.exe
  6. Click Next to select scope tags (Optional)
  7. Click Next to select applicable Groups
  8. Click Next to Review and Create -> to review the information entered earlier is correct
  9. Save to add the rule.

Option 2: Using Group Policy Object (GPO) for domain environments

  1. Open the "Group Policy Management" console (gpmc.msc).
  2. Create a new GPO or edit an existing GPO that is linked to the Organizational Units (OUs) containing the computers you want to configure.
  3. Navigate to Computer Configuration > Policies > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security > "Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security - Local Group Policy Object" > "Outbound Rules".
  4. Right click Outbound Rules and select New Rule...
  5. Select Program as the rule type and click Next.
  6. Select This program path, %systemroot%\System32\mshta.exe, and select Next.
  7. Select Block the connection and select Next.
  8. For the Profile step, ensure Domain, Private, and Public are checked. Select Next.
  9. Type a name for the rule (for example, Block mshta.exe outbound via GPO) and an optional description. Select Finish.
  10. Ensure the GPO is linked and enforced on the desired OUs.
  11. For 64-bit systems, repeat steps 2-10 with this program path: %systemroot%\SysWOW64\mshta.exe in step 6.
  12. Type: gpupdate /force.

Option 3: Using Windows Defender Firewall GUI Console (per machine)

Use this option only for standalone devices or environments where locally created firewall rules are allowed.
  1. Open "Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security". You can search for it in the Start menu.
  2. In the left pane, click on "Outbound Rules".
  3. In the right pane, click on "New Rule...".
  4. Select "Program" as the rule type and click "Next".
  5. Select "This program path" and enter or browse to %systemroot%\System32\mshta.exe. Click "Next".
  6. Select "Block the connection" and click "Next".
  7. Ensure all profiles (Domain, Private, Public) are checked. Click "Next".
  8. Enter a name for the rule (e.g., "Block mshta.exe outbound connections") and an optional description. Click "Finish".
  9. For 64-bit systems, repeat steps 3-8 with this program path: %systemroot%\SysWOW64\mshta.exe in step 5.

If devices in your network use Telnet, either switch to a more secure protocol such as SSH, disable the server altogether, or apply network access restrictions if the first two options aren’t possible.

If devices in your network use SNMP V1 or V2, either switch to a more secure protocol such as SNMP V3, or disable them altogether. If neither of those option are feasible, apply network access restrictions

  • Click SETTINGS
  • Click ENABLE ACCESS BASED ENUMERATION
